open_questions: Whether he sits behind the beat. The repo's Back in Black library note says the snare sits late; no source found measures it, and the 2000 interview speaks of locking with Malcolm and Cliff, not of laying back. The style plays him on the beat.

The kits on each record: the Songsterr track names (Slingerland in 1975-1976, Gretsch in 1977-1979, Sonor from 1980) are the transcribers' labels; the 2000 interview gives Sonor, one rack tom, two floor toms and a 24-inch kick.
His own words at length: the Cyber Drum interview (2000) is read through a fan repost; no Modern Drummer or Rhythm interview with him was found to read.
Whether the 1979 promo film is mirrored: it shows his tattoo on the right arm, a 1996 photograph on the left.

identity.name: Phil Rudd
identity.summary: AC/DC's drummer from 1975 to 1983 and from 1994: the pocket, and next to nothing else. Eighths on the hats, the kick on 1 and 3, the snare hard on 2 and 4, a crash on the first bar of a phrase, almost no fills; locked to Malcolm Young's rhythm guitar and Cliff Williams' bass, with no click ('you can't rock to a click'). The band said a groove went missing when he left, and came back when he did.

traditions.tradition: Melbourne pub rock: Buster Brown and the Coloured Balls
traditions.impact: Buster Brown with Angry Anderson (Something to Say, 1974), then Lobby Loyde's Coloured Balls, before AC/DC's audition.

traditions.tradition: British beat and rock: the Small Faces
traditions.impact: Tin Soldier was his first inspiration, the band's breakdown into the guitar (Cyber Drum, 2000).

formative_events.event: Auditioned for AC/DC in Melbourne in January 1975, told of it by Trevor Young; 'I turned up, played and was offered the job.'
Left the band after his parts for Flick of the Switch, partly over a conflict with Malcolm Young; to New Zealand, helicopters and a farm.
Back in AC/DC after Big Gun: the band said 'a certain groove had been missing' since he left.

eras.label: The Albert Studios records
eras.context: Sydney with Vanda and Young, then London: T.N.T., Dirty Deeds, Let There Be Rock.
defining_traits: eighths on the hats over 1 and 3

eras.label: The Mutt Lange records
eras.context: Highway to Hell in London, Back in Black in the Bahamas, For Those About to Rock: the sound a generation learned rock drumming from.
defining_traits: the hats half-open on the beat
the kick on the "and" of 3 or 4

eras.label: The return
eras.context: Ballbreaker to Power Up; Black Ice with Brendan O'Brien in Vancouver, the drums in a small booth.
defining_traits: the hats leaned on the beat

swing.notes: Straight eighths throughout; The Jack is a slow 12/8 blues.

dynamics.balance: A loud, even backbeat; the tabs write no ghost notes ('let someone else worry about ghost notes', Drumeo); the hats loosened or tightened from song to song.

feel_profile.interaction: Locked to Malcolm Young's rhythm guitar and the bass: 'we all lock together to get the groove' (2000). No click: the records drift where the riff takes them, It's a Long Way to the Top from 131 to 138, Hells Bells from 94 to 110.

hand_techniques.name: eighths on the hats
hand_techniques.description: Eighths on the hats with the right hand, loose or tight from song to song: half-open on the beat (Highway to Hell), open on the beat (the bagpipe parts), open for a chorus (Back in Black).

hand_techniques.name: the crash on the backbeat
hand_techniques.description: The right hand leaves the hats for the crash on 2 and 4 with the snare (Hells Bells), or crashes with the kick on 1, 2 and 3 (T.N.T., Dirty Deeds).

hand_techniques.name: the floor tom in eighths
hand_techniques.description: The right hand on the floor tom under a riff (Dirty Deeds).

foot_techniques.name: single foot, on 1 and 3
foot_techniques.description: One 24-inch bass drum on 1 and 3, sometimes on every beat (T.N.T., Let There Be Rock, Rock 'n' Roll Train), sometimes pushed to the "and" of 3 or 4.

searched: The ten Songsterr tabs read section by section, It's a Long Way to the Top to Rock 'n' Roll Train
Wikipedia (Phil Rudd, AC/DC and the albums), the Cyber Drum interview (2000), Modern Drummer (2011), Drumeo, Bonedo, Sound On Sound (2009), Joe Daly
devices_search.note: None found, and none expected: he is the drummer who plays no device. Back in Black's turn in groups of three is a fill of a bar's end, not a cross-rhythm carried through a phrase.

voice_language.snare: Hard on 2 and 4, a beefy crack, no ghost notes; moved to 1 and the "and" of 3 once (Dirty Deeds).
voice_language.kick: On 1 and 3, or every beat; pushed to the "and" of 3 (You Shook Me All Night Long) or of 4 (Highway to Hell).
voice_language.toms: Hardly at all: the floor tom in eighths under Dirty Deeds, a pair at the end of a fill.
voice_language.hihat: Eighths, from tight to washing open; half-open on the beat in Highway to Hell, open on the beat in It's a Long Way to the Top.
voice_language.cymbals: A crash on the first bar of a phrase, on the backbeat in Hells Bells, with the kick on 1, 2 and 3 in a chorus.

aesthetic: a fat snare crack and a big 24-inch kick
sound_profile.cymbal_character: Paiste 2002s by Bonedo's account: 14-inch medium hats, washing when loosened.

by_era.description: Albert Studios with Vanda and Young: dry and boxy, the kick and snare forward.
Tony Platt's Back in Black: close mics, gated, pitched down a little, not compressed.
Black Ice: a small booth inside the live room; 'they don't like things roomy or bombastic' (Mike Fraser).

sample_hints.1975-1977: Big Rusty: a damped 24-inch kick and a wooden snare played hard, under a wash of cymbal.
sample_hints.1979-2008: Studio rock: tight, dry and close, like the Lange records and Black Ice.

signature_traits.label: The pocket and nothing else
signature_traits.description: Eighths on the hats, the kick on 1 and 3, the snare on 2 and 4, for a whole song.

signature_traits.label: Hats loosened and tightened
signature_traits.description: Half-open on the beat, open on the beat, open for a chorus: the hats set the song's colour.

signature_traits.label: The kick on every beat
signature_traits.description: The kick on all four under the backbeat, with no hats (T.N.T.) or under the hats leaned on the beat (Rock 'n' Roll Train).

signature_traits.label: Almost no fills
signature_traits.description: A turn at the end of a part, the band's hits played with the band, and nothing else.

patterns.name: It's a Long Way to the Top: the verse
patterns.function: Eighths on the hats, the kick on 1 and 3, the snare on 2 and 4: the whole song

patterns.name: It's a Long Way to the Top: the bagpipes
patterns.function: The hats opened on every beat and shut on the "and"

patterns.name: T.N.T.: the second verse
patterns.function: The kick on every beat, the snare on 2 and 4, no hats

evidence.note: The first verse, under the chant, is the kick alone on every beat.

patterns.name: T.N.T.: the chorus
patterns.function: Crashes on 1, 2 and 3 over the backbeat, then a bar of eighths on the hats

patterns.name: The Jack: the shuffle
patterns.function: A slow 12/8 blues: every triplet on the hats, the kick on 1, the last triplet of 1, the last of 2, 3, the last of 3 and of 4

evidence.note: The tab is 4/4 at 77 in eighth-note triplets; written here in 12/8, its tempo in quarters.

patterns.name: The Jack: the hits
patterns.function: The crash and the snare on every pulse, the kick on the two triplets after each

patterns.name: Dirty Deeds Done Dirt Cheap: the riff
patterns.function: Eighths on the floor tom, the kick on 1, 3 and its "and", the snare on 2 and 4

patterns.name: Dirty Deeds Done Dirt Cheap: the verse
patterns.function: The floor tom in eighths, the kick on every beat, the snare moved to 1 and the "and" of 3

patterns.name: Let There Be Rock: the verse
patterns.function: The kick on every beat at 180, eighths on the hats

patterns.name: Let There Be Rock: the solos
patterns.function: Open hats washing in eighths over the kick on every beat

patterns.name: Highway to Hell: the verse
patterns.function: The hats half-open on the beat and shut on the "and", the kick on 1, 3 and the "and" of 4

patterns.name: Highway to Hell: the chorus
patterns.function: A crash on 1 and the hats open; the next bar the hats open to 3, crashes on 3 and 4

patterns.name: Hells Bells: the chorus
patterns.function: The crash on 2 and 4 with the snare, the hats between

patterns.name: Hells Bells: the solo
patterns.function: The kick on the "and" of 1, 2 and 3, a crash on the "and" of 2

patterns.name: Back in Black: the verse
patterns.function: Eighths on the hats, the kick on 1 and 3, the snare on 2 and 4, nothing else

patterns.name: Back in Black: the turn
patterns.function: Every fourth bar: threes from the "and" of 2, the snare, then the kick under an open hat

patterns.name: Back in Black: the chorus
patterns.function: A crash on 1, then the hats left open for the bar

patterns.name: You Shook Me All Night Long: the verse
patterns.function: The second kick moved off 3 to its "and"

patterns.name: You Shook Me All Night Long: the chorus
patterns.function: The crash and the kick on 1 and 2, the snare on 4 alone; then the plain beat

evidence.note: Robert Christgau called the song 'a drum-hooked fucksong' (Wikipedia).

patterns.name: Rock 'n' Roll Train: the verse
patterns.function: The kick on every beat, the hats accented on the beat and light on the "and"

patterns.name: Rock 'n' Roll Train: the chorus
patterns.function: A crash on 1, then the hats open over the kick on every beat

equipment.label: A dark kit with chrome hardware, the Highway to Hell film, 1979
equipment.layout_notes: The 1979 promotional film: dark shells, chrome stands, white heads, brass cymbals; one rack tom and floor toms. The Songsterr tab of the song names a Gretsch kit.

equipment.label: Sonor, 2000
equipment.layout_notes: One rack tom, two large floor toms, a 24-inch bass drum and a 5 3/4-inch snare (Cyber Drum, 2000). Sonor Phonic drums and Paiste 2002 cymbals by Bonedo's account of Back in Black.

affiliations.name: AC/DC
affiliations.notes: 1975 to 1983, 1994 to 2015, and from 2018 (Power Up, 2020). Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, 2003.

affiliations.name: Buster Brown
affiliations.notes: With Angry Anderson; Something to Say (1974).

evidence.note: His first inspiration was the Small Faces' Tin Soldier, the breakdown into the guitar (Cyber Drum, 2000); Kenney Jones played the drums on it.
'The rhythm section is Cliff, Malcolm and myself and we all lock together to get the groove' (2000); the 1983 split came partly from a conflict with Malcolm.
'You couldn't find a more solid person or drummer than Phil Rudd' (Hit Parader, 1983).
Clack was fired in January 1975; after Ron Carpenter and Russell Coleman, Rudd joined that month from Buster Brown.
AC/DC's drummer from 1983. Rudd: 'Simon Wright didn't do a bad job.'
On The Razors Edge (1989-1994) before Rudd came back, and on the 2015-2016 tour when he could not.
Currenti's two High Voltage tracks sit on T.N.T. beside Rudd's seven.

philosophy.idea: Lock in with the rhythm guitar and the bass; nobody plays by himself.
Feel the whole song and play for it, not to show off: the fast fills came first, the feel after.
Tune by feel: each drum answers in a narrow range of tunings.

innovations: The hard rock backbeat at its plainest: the drum part of AC/DC, copied by every rock drummer since

cultural_references.description: Modern Drummer: 'the very definition of rock drumming'; Kenny Aronoff and Eric Singer: 'the heart and soul of AC/DC'.
Lars Ulrich: 'I also love people like Phil Rudd ... they make it swing, they make it move.'
Rock and Roll Hall of Fame with AC/DC, 2003.

common_misconceptions: That anyone could play it: the parts are simple, the feel is not, and the band said a groove went missing without him.
That he drums on Thunderstruck and Moneytalks: they are Chris Slade's, on The Razors Edge.

beatbreaker.default_kit_sound: Big Rusty for the Albert Studios records; a tight, dry studio rock kit for the Lange records and Black Ice
generation_rules: Eighths on the hats, the kick on 1 and 3, the snare on 2 and 4; a crash on the first bar of a phrase.
The kick on every beat for the faster songs, or pushed to the "and" of 3 or of 4.
The hats loosened or tightened by song: half-open on the beat, open on the beat, open after a chorus crash.
Almost no fills: a turn at the end of a part, and only there.

lineage_display.lineage_blurb: The Small Faces' Tin Soldier first; then the drum part every hard rock drummer learns, Lars Ulrich and Tomas Haake among those who name him.
